findings.reason: The first real CPython 3.13 smoke reached a valid wheel and installed manifest but compared the stable CLI string `pocketchat 1.1.0` directly with the metadata version `1.1.0`. A red regression now freezes the existing prefix format and validation compares its normalized version value.

Two real builds produced different ZIP container SHA-256 values while their canonical package manifests were identical. The docs now claim manifest determinism only and explicitly do not claim reproducible wheel container bytes.

Apple Command Line Tools CPython 3.9.6 with pip 21.2.4 built UNKNOWN-0.0.0 even after an isolated setuptools 82 environment; the explicit non-isolated fallback used setuptools 58.0.4 below the repository requirement. Unit coverage passed on 3.9, but a valid CPython 3.9 wheel/install smoke remains unverified in this local toolchain.

`ruff check pocketchat tests` remains red on repository-wide style rules: the unmodified baseline reports 2265 findings and this candidate reports 2263. The actual CI E9/F gate passes for the changed script/test, and the changed test file passes full Ruff; unrelated baseline modernization findings were not changed.

Round 3 completed an independent fresh-context review of the implementation, tests, docs and the new fix diff. It reproduced and closed PM-6 with no open blocker/major. Exact-candidate CI and public main integration remain separate gates.

Independent review reproduced two linked integrity gaps: a nested pocketchat/evil.dist-info/INSTALLER path was treated as installation-generated and disappeared from the manifest, and a nested pocketchat/evil.dist-info/RECORD was excluded from wheel/install comparison, allowing payload drift. The fix admits only generated metadata directly under the selected pocketchat-<version>.dist-info root, excludes only that root's RECORD from pair comparison, rejects non-canonical source and manifest paths, mismatched categories and dist-info/version drift, and adds regression coverage for nested payload retention, nested RECORD drift refusal and extra dist-info refusal.
